tools.name: make_game
tools.description: Starts generation of a small browser game about one person from the sender's supplied habits or inside jokes. Returns immediately with build progress. Games are free within a daily allowance. When the assistant allowance runs out, returns an OAuth sign-in request or a handoff URL. It never charges a

tools.name: get_made_game
tools.description: Returns the current stage of a game generation job identified by its private idempotency key. A completed job includes the title, cast, recipient play link and sender management link. Management links grant private sender access.

tools.name: get_gift_catalog
tools.description: Returns the supported formats, capabilities, requirements and limits for saving custom HTML games as private drafts.

tools.name: create_custom_game
tools.description: Saves a supplied self-contained HTML game as a free private draft. Returns a preview URL and private management token. Accepted games have inline code and embedded assets, keyboard and touch controls, a goal and restart. Network requests, payments and personal-data collection are prohibited. Repeate

tools.name: revise_custom_game
tools.description: Replaces an existing private draft with supplied HTML and game details. Requires the draft's management token and current revision number. A stale expectedRevision is rejected to prevent overwriting another edit.

tools.name: get_gift
tools.description: Returns a private draft's metadata, current revision, preview link and status for the supplied management token. Game HTML is excluded.

tools.name: get_gift_history
tools.description: Returns the last five retained revisions of a private draft for the supplied management token. Revision metadata may contain the sender's personal content. Game HTML is excluded.

tools.name: export_gift
tools.description: Returns a private draft as portable JSON containing its complete self-contained game HTML. The recipient's email address and private tokens are excluded. An optional revision number selects a retained revision instead of the current version.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "make_game" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_gift_catalog, get_gift, get_gift_history · Private data: get_made_game, get_gift_catalog, create_custom_game, revise_custom_game, get_gift, get_gift_history, export_gift · Public sink: export_gift.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_gift_catalog, get_gift, get_gift_history · Private data: get_made_game, get_gift_catalog, create_custom_game, revise_custom_game, get_gift, get_gift_history, export_gift · Public sink: export_gift

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "make_game" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
